q: I guess I’m just looking for some comfort, some testimonies of other mums who went threw the same. I feel like we are doing such a bad job, and I am so exhausted.
cx: 21-month-old wakes 5-10 times a night since crawling at 6 months; signs off 'a broken hearted mum'.

q: Appreciate the sweet words, but yes it’s like day and night when I speak to some of my friends who have sleepers. I’m also home with my baby.
cx: Comparing with friends' babies.

q: We have tried night weaning her and it worked for a while but she’s the worst baby when it come to teething.
cx: Teething undid night weaning.

q: He has been an independent sleeper since he was around six months old, using principles from *Precious Little Sleep*. For more than two years, we have been able to complete his bedtime routine, say goodnight, leave the room while he was awake, and let him fall asleep independently.

q: The change roughly coincided with two major things: we had just spent three weeks together on vacation, and he recently started preschool/daycare.
cx: Same post.

q: How long would you give a gradual approach before changing course?
cx: One of a list of exact-steps questions.

q: We would especially appreciate detailed experiences from families whose previously independent toddler suddenly began needing parental presence at both bedtime and overnight.
cx: Wants matching cases, not general advice.

q: my husband got up with me and tried so hard to get her to sleep but she was crying to the point of throwing up when with him. At that point, it just made sense to put her back on the boob.
cx: Exclusively breastfed 5.5-month-old up every hour; husband can do day naps only.

q: When were you able to transition away from nursing to sleep without baby becoming hysterical? I'm so tired, I just want some time for myself beyond the hour or two my husband can offer before my baby needs me again.
cx: Same post.
